ticket.title: task_updated writes the event log but never refreshes the ticket projection, so 8 of 166 root tickets serve a description their projection does not hold
ticket.description: A ticket file is a projection plus an event log, and the projection is supposed to be the materialised current state. It is written when the ticket is created and NOT refreshed by task_updated: `storypole update --desc` / `--append-desc` append an event and leave the projection as it was. Measured 2026-11-10 on the root store: 8 of 166 tickets serve a description that differs from their projection, 6 of them with an entirely empty projection because the description arrived after creation (the defer-then-update flow GB-347 itself went through). Readers disagree as a result: `storypole show` replays and shows the real text, while anything that reads the JSON projection - including `remint` dry run citation counts and any script - sees the stale or empty one. `update` should write the projection it just changed, or the store should expose one rebuild that guarantees projection == replay. Found while proving GB-347: it is why remint citation rewrites landed on a field nothing serves.
